the anisotropy of the inelastic scattering of gas mixture components and the selectivity of diffusion are determined by the ratio of the cross sections for inelastic scattering of radiation by the components of the gas mixture and the ratio of diffusion coefficients for these components.
the anisotropy of collisional processes in the presence of a laser beam can be used to selectively separate gas mixture components in a diffusion process.
the diffusion of a binary gas mixture is anisotropic, and the diffusion of a mixture component is selective in the collisional diffusion regime.

the study of the influence of laser radiation on gas mixture components in a diffusion regime.
the development of a new method for selective gas separation and purification, which is based on the use of laser radiation and the anisotropy of gas scattering in the inelastic regime.
the interaction of laser radiation with a gas mixture.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anisotropy of the collision cross section is the key to the understanding of the mechanism of selective diffusion.
the anisotropy of the inelastic scattering of radiation is a necessary condition for the selective diffusion of gas components.
the laser radiation intensity is the key parameter for the gas mixture components separation in the collisional and diffusion regimes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diffusion coefficient is anisotropic and depends on the direction of the laser beam.

the diffusion of a mixture of two gases in the presence of a laser field may be different in the case of excitation of only one of the gases, even when the laser intensity is extremely low and the laser radiation does not affect the diffusion process directly.
